Corporate.brandDescription: Wendover Cannabis Holdings operates a portfolio of cannabis cultivation, manufacturing, and retail brands across multiple state markets.

Corporate.mission: To provide a serious operating platform for mid-tier cannabis brands that want to keep their identity and outsource the operations.
Corporate.vision: A multi-state cannabis operator whose portfolio brands grow under their own names because the operations and compliance are shared.
coreValues: Senior — partners deal with partners.
Operational — compliance and licensing run on schedule.
Reliable — predictable supply across states.
Discreet — brand relationships stay private.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Wendover is a real American place-name common across the western United States, with a holding-company register. Cannabis Holdings follows the multi-state operator naming convention used in the cannabis industry (Trulieve, Curaleaf, Cresco Labs structure). The pair reads as an institutional operator with multi-brand, multi-state portfolio scale.
Corporate.manifesto: Wendover Cannabis Holdings owns and operates a portfolio of cannabis brands across cultivation, manufacturing, and retail categories. Each brand retains its identity, brand-team leadership, and customer relationships; we operate the shared compliance, licensing, supply chain, and back office. The buyer is a cannabis brand founder considering sale, a multi-state retailer seeking single-vendor supply relationships, or an institutional investor holding cannabis assets.
Corporate.industrySummary: Cannabis has consolidated under a small number of multi-state operators (Curaleaf, Trulieve, Cresco Labs, GTI). The opening underneath is for a regional mid-tier multi-brand operator with deep compliance operations and the procurement-grade reliability dispensary networks and institutional investors require.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Curaleaf (curaleaf.com) is the multi-state cannabis operator reference. Trulieve (trulieve.com) holds the multi-state peer slot. Cresco Labs (crescolabs.com) sits in the multi-state mid-tier peer position. Green Thumb Industries (gtigrows.com) plays the multi-state peer reference. We belong in the regional mid-tier multi-state cannabis operator category.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Wendover Cannabis Holdings is a regional multi-state multi-brand cannabis operator running cultivation, manufacturing, retail, and shared compliance across a portfolio of brands.
Corporate.positioningRationale: We compete on shared compliance infrastructure, multi-state licensing reach, and the operational reliability brand founders and institutional investors need in a regulated industry.

Creative.tagline: A cannabis brand for the longer afternoon.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Slow Sunday is a phrase about the right pace for a weekend afternoon — phrase as brand name, with the Co. suffix grounding it in considered-modern DTC convention.
Creative.manifesto: Most cannabis brands sell wellness, luxury, or counterculture. We made Good Couch because the truth about cannabis is that most of it ends with someone on a couch, lights low, eating something they didn't plan to eat. The brand is for the small private hour. The lights are dim. The phone is face-down. The couch is good.
Creative.industrySummary: Cannabis branding has been split between wellness theatre and youth-culture posturing. There's room for a brand that's warm, honest, sticker-friendly, and serious about the actual relaxed experience the customer is paying for.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Houseplant (houseplant.com) does design-led restraint. Cann (drinkcann.com) holds the beverage middle. Old Pal (oldpal.com) sits in the friend-with-weed peer position. We sit warmer and more honest about the couch.
Creative.positioningStatement: A cannabis brand for the small couch hour after dinner.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 50. Uses cannabis occasionally, almost always at home, almost always on a couch. Buys the brand because the marketing made them feel seen rather than upsold.

dos: Talk about the couch, the snack, the movie
Quote real customer evenings
Speak softly
donts: Photograph models in linen at sunset

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark in a punchy display serif with the O of GOOD stylized as a small filled circle, like a lamp from above. Standalone lamp-O icon for stickers, social profiles, and the back of every package.

Creative.tagline: A cannabis brand for the people who don't want to talk about it.
Creative.brandDescription: The Quiet Cabinet Co is a creative-led cannabis brand designed for discreet domestic use — packaging that lives quietly in the medicine cabinet, products meant for the evening at home.
Creative.scope:
The Quiet Cabinet Co works across:
• Pre-roll and tincture products in discreet packaging
• Single-serving formats for predictable dosing
• Domestic-aesthetic packaging that fits the medicine cabinet
• Quarterly published essays on quiet domestic use
• Subscription-based home delivery in select states
Creative.mission: To make cannabis fit quietly into the household, without theatre.
Creative.vision: A cannabis brand whose packaging looks at home next to the toothpaste, with no one noticing.
coreValues: Considered — packaging respects the household.
Warm — products fit into evening domestic rituals.
Discreet — the brand does not shout.
Literary — the writing about quiet use is part of the brand.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The Quiet Cabinet is a phrase about the household storage space for personal use — a small domestic position that the brand stakes for cannabis. The definite article + Co suffix follows the considered-creative trade-name school (The Pantry Project, The Reading Light Co). The brand argues for cannabis as a domestic, unremarkable household item.
Creative.manifesto: Most cannabis branding shouts — the leaf, the green, the playful illustration, the bright packaging. We started The Quiet Cabinet Co because actual domestic use is the opposite of shouted. Customers want products that fit quietly in the cabinet beside the toothpaste, with single-serving formats and predictable dosing. The brand is the quiet.
Creative.industrySummary: Cannabis branding has converged on either bright recreational or wellness-aesthetic packaging. There is real space for a creative-led brand that argues for cannabis as a quiet domestic product — discreet packaging, single-serving formats, predictable dosing.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Dosist (dosist.com) plays the closest peer in dosed-format minimal cannabis. Beboe (beboe.com) holds the considered-aesthetic peer slot. Lord Jones (lordjones.com) sits in the wellness-aesthetic peer position. Mary's Medicinals (maryswellness.com) plays the dosed-medical reference. We sit alongside Dosist with a stronger domestic-quiet position.
Creative.positioningStatement: The Quiet Cabinet Co is a cannabis brand designed for discreet domestic use, with single-serving formats and packaging that lives quietly in the household.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand competes on the domestic position. Packaging, products, and voice all argue for cannabis as an unremarkable household item.

targetAudience.primary: Adults 32-55 who use cannabis quietly at home and want products that fit into the household.
behaviors: Use cannabis for sleep, evening unwinding, or quiet domestic moments.
Care about packaging aesthetics matching their home.
Want single-serving formats for predictable dosing.
Prefer discretion over conversation about use.
motivations: Want cannabis that fits quietly into the household.
Want predictable single-serving dosing.
Want a brand that doesn't shout.

dos: Photograph products in domestic settings — the cabinet, the nightstand, the kitchen drawer.

Describe products by use moment, not by recreational language.
Sign correspondence by the founder.

Creative.tagline: A cannabis brand built around the paper.
Creative.brandDescription: Rolling Paper Co is a creative-led cannabis brand specializing in considered rolling papers and the rolling tradition, with flower sold as a secondary product alongside the papers.
Creative.scope:
Rolling Paper Co works across:
• Considered rolling papers as the primary product
• Cannabis flower sold alongside the papers
• Custom papers commissioned from heritage paper mills
• Quarterly published essays on the rolling tradition
• Annual rolling-craft gathering
Creative.mission: To restore the rolling paper as the central object of cannabis ritual.
Creative.vision: A brand whose rolling papers become a reference for serious rollers.
coreValues: Warm — the paper is part of the ritual.
Specific — every paper's specs are documented.
Considered — the roll is the work.
Literary — the writing about rolling is part of the brand.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Rolling Paper is the universal cannabis-trade phrase for the thin paper used to roll joints — naming the brand after the artefact rather than the substance. Co is the small-firm suffix. No 'The' prefix.
Creative.manifesto: Most cannabis brands centre the flower. We started Rolling Paper Co because the actual most considered ritual object is the paper — the gauge, the gum, the burn, the way the smoke moves through it.
Creative.industrySummary: Rolling papers are typically commoditized. There is real space for a creative-led brand that explicitly positions on paper craft.
Creative.competitorLandscape: RAW (rawthentic.com) plays the heritage paper peer. OCB (ocb.net) holds the heritage paper peer slot. Elements (elementsrollingpapers.com) sits in the considered peer position. We sit alongside RAW with sharper craft focus.
Creative.positioningStatement: Rolling Paper Co is a cannabis brand specializing in considered rolling papers and the rolling tradition.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand competes on the paper-craft premise.
